_comment: Baseline for check-body-completeness.mjs, keyed check -> bucket -> count. The gate fires on GROWTH in a bucket or on ANY NEW bucket. Shrink these numbers as the backlog is worked off; never raise one without saying why here and in the commit message.  CHAMBER_SIZE_MISMATCH is keyed state|direction, because the two directions need OPPOSITE fixes. Seeded 2026-11-14 at 19 of the 514 chambers that state a size; 18 after CC_0430. 948 of 1,462 chambers state NO size (NULL, or the 0 sentinel that 296 carry) and are invisible here -- the honest limit of this check s reach, not a clean result.  🔴 ALL 14 too_many ROWS WERE TRIAGED ON 2026-11-14 AND ONLY THREE ARE CANDIDATE DEFECTS. official_count DOES NOT HAVE ONE DEFINITION ACROSS THE CORPUS, and that is the single most important thing to know before reading this bucket. Bangor s 9 INCLUDED its council-chosen mayor; El Monte s 6, Inglewood s 4, Pasadena s 7, DeKalb s 3, Fulton s 4 and three Texas cities EXCLUDE a separately-elected mayor or executive. Same column, opposite conventions. So a surplus of exactly 1 that matches an exec-type office is a DEFINITIONAL mismatch, not a defect.    (a) SURPLUS IS A SEPARATELY-ELECTED EXECUTIVE -- 8 rows, not defects: ca|too_many Pasadena (7/8), El Monte (6/7), Inglewood (4/5); ga|too_many DeKalb (3/4), Fulton (4/5); tx|too_many Blue Ridge, Weston, Josephine (5/6 each). Each holds a Mayor or county executive their official_count does not count.    (b) EMPTY ROWS AWAITING AN ELECTION -- 3 rows, not defects:     ca|too_many Santa Clarita (states 5, holds 8, FIVE people). ⚠ EARLIER NOTES IN THIS FILE AND IN PR #1472 CALLED THIS THE MOST LIKELY REAL DEFECT AND THAT WAS WRONG. It is the CVRA staggered by-district conversion CLAUDE.md documents: 3 legacy At-Large holdovers still legitimately in office + 5 by-district successors, of which D1 and D3 are seated and D2, D4 and D5 are empty. Checked the way CLAUDE.md says to -- READ ITS RACES, do not reason from the count: each empty row carries exactly ONE race, all three in the 2026 LA County General of 2026-11-03, seats=1, candidates filed and ALL still candidate_status=active, so NO winner is recorded yet. All three carry their CC_0299 voter-facing description. Sitting at-large member Laurene Weste is herself a candidate in District 4, which is the conversion visibly in progress. 🔴 CC_0298 called this shape duplicate seats and was wrong in a way that would have justified deleting real offices; do not repeat it. ▶ Resolves when the December 2026 pass seats the winners and retires the at-large holdovers -- NOT before LA County certifies.     us|too_many US Attorney General (1/2) and Secretary of Homeland Security (1/2): each carries a second office row with NO current holder. Not investigated.    (c) UNEXPLAINED -- 3 rows, and these are where to look first:     ~~ma|too_many Cambridge~~ ✅ RESOLVED 2026-11-14 by CC_0431 -- see the note at the end.     ~~tn|too_many Nashville and tx|too_many Lowry Crossing~~ ✅ BOTH RESOLVED 2026-11-14 -- see the notes at the end. (c) IS NOW EMPTY: every one of the 14 too_many rows is classified.    TOO FEW -- the body has seats we do not hold. Lewiston s shape:     sc|too_few Columbia (7/6), Myrtle Beach (7/6); tx|too_few Plano (9/8); al|too_few Alabama State Board of Education (9/8).     (me|too_few Lewiston was here and is REMOVED -- see the CC_0430 note below.)  DISTRICT_WITHOUT_OFFICE is keyed state|district_type. Seeded 2026-11-14 at 3,207 of 11,403 districts. 3,053 are COUNTY rows: 21 states hold no county offices at all and no state has a complete county tier. Keying on state|district_type lets an unseeded state sit still while a wave that creates an unseated office in it fires immediately. me|COUNTY 16 is the finding that prompted this gate -- every Maine county is a district with a polygon and zero offices, found by CC_0428 s own reachability gate failing (ROSTERS.md R9k). NOT a defect to fix by deleting; a tier nobody has seeded.  WATCH THESE TWO: 25|LOCAL 1 and 25|SCHOOL 1 are Massachusetts districts carrying FIPS 25 where every other row carries USPS. The state key is deliberately NOT normalised -- mapping 25 -> ma would launder exactly the defect class this gate exists to surface. Fixing those two rows should REMOVE both buckets, not lower them.  2026-11-14 (CC_0430): me|too_few (was 1) REMOVED, not lowered -- Lewiston School Committee now holds 9 offices against its official_count of 9. The ninth seat (City Council Representative, is_appointed_position = true) was created and seated with Ward 3 Councillor Scott A. Harriman. Verified on prod: 9 offices, 9 distinct current holders, 0 empty seats, 238 unflagged drift baseline unmoved. Any reappearance should fire as a NEW bucket. ⚠ That seat is re-elected ANNUALLY and the council s term for it expires 2027-01-04: if the council elects a different member this bucket does NOT move -- nine against nine either way -- so the HOLDER changes and nothing here notices.  2026-11-14 (CC_0431): ma|too_many STAYS AT 1 and that is the right outcome -- Cambridge moved OUT of the unexplained pile, it did not leave the bucket. It read 9 stated / 11 offices / TEN people, which is South Portland s more-rows-than-people signature. Both bodies own words settled it: cambridgema.gov says "There are nine members on the City Council, including the Mayor and Vice Mayor", and cpsd.us says "Six members are elected at large", "The Committee s Chair is elected by the seven members", "The Mayor, who is elected by the nine elected City Council members, also serves on the School Committee." So the Mayor was modelled BACKWARDS: a tenth council row she did not have, and no committee seat she did. CC_0431 deleted the council Mayor row (DELETE not retitle, by CC_0428 s test: all nine councillor rows were held by nine different people, so deleting unseats nobody) and created School Committee Member (Mayor), seated with Siddiqui from 2026-01-05. The committee is now 7/7. Cambridge now reads 9 stated / 10 offices / 10 DISTINCT PEOPLE: the residue is City Manager, Cambridge s appointed chief executive, who is not a council member -- so it belongs with the exec-type class in (a) above, not in (c). 🔴 WHETHER AN APPOINTED EXECUTIVE BELONGS IN A LEGISLATIVE CHAMBER IS A QUESTION ABOUT ALL NINE OF THOSE ROWS, NOT ABOUT CAMBRIDGE, and it is not decided. ▶ So (c) UNEXPLAINED is now just Nashville Metro Council (40/41) and Lowry Crossing TX (5/9).  ⚠ FOUND BY CC_0431 S OWN GATE FAILING, NOT FIXED: production carries 57 politicians.office_id values pointing at offices that no longer exist. That column has NO foreign key, so every past delete that skipped the repoint left one. The first draft of CC_0431 gated on that total being zero and the dry run refused it -- which is the delta-not-total rule catching its own author. CC_0431 gates its own delta instead and leaves the 57 alone.  2026-11-14 (Nashville, NO MIGRATION NEEDED): tn|too_many is the exec-type class, not a defect. nashville.gov/departments/council: "The Vice Mayor serves as the president of the Council, which is comprised of 35 district members and five members serving at-large." 35 + 5 = 40 = official_count, which is CORRECT; the 41st row is the Vice Mayor (Angie Emery Henderson, confirmed current on the same page), elected county-wide as the Council s presiding officer and not one of the 40. Nothing to change. ⚠ Her office carries is_appointed_position = NULL rather than false -- left alone deliberately, because 3,396 offices repo-wide carry NULL and fixing this one would be arbitrary. That NULL publishes as is_elected = NULL, which is a repo-wide question worth someone s attention.  2026-11-14 (CC_0432): tx|too_many STAYS AT 4 and Lowry Crossing stays in it, with a surplus of ONE instead of four. official_count was 5 against NINE offices held by NINE distinct people -- so the rows were right and the count was wrong. The city s own council page lists exactly our nine: Mayor Pat Kelly, then two councilmembers under each of Ward 1-4. 🔴 WHERE THE 5 CAME FROM, MEASURED: exactly four Texas council chambers carry official_count 5 and all four are small Collin County towns -- Blue Ridge, Josephine, Weston and this one. The other three hold Mayor + 5 = 6 offices, so 5 is right for them; it is Texas s general-law default of five aldermen. ▶ A DEFAULT THAT IS RIGHT THREE TIMES OUT OF FOUR LOOKS LIKE A SOURCED FIGURE. Set to 8, not 9, so it keeps the same meaning its three siblings use (councilmembers, excluding the mayor).  🔴 TWO LOWRY CROSSING FINDINGS LEFT OPEN ON PURPOSE, BOTH IN CC_0432 S HEADER: (1) Places 5-8 -- Madrid, Rios, Cash, Simpson -- carry district_id NULL, so FOUR SITTING COUNCILMEMBERS ARE UNREACHABLE FROM EVERY ADDRESS while Places 1-4 and the Mayor point at the city-wide district; (2) our titles say Place and the city says Ward, with an exact mapping (Places 1-4 are each ward s first-listed member, 5-8 the second). BOTH FIXES TURN ON ONE UNANSWERED QUESTION -- are the wards ELECTORATES or RESIDENCY QUALIFICATIONS? R9i settled exactly that question the OTHER way for South Portland, so it cannot be assumed. Guessing picks between showing a voter seven councillors who do not represent them and hiding four who do.  ⚠ AND A TRAP WORTH REPEATING: searching for Lowry Crossing s council composition returned ecode360 pages that read decisively and AGREED WITH OUR ROW COUNT -- they are City of Garland (custId GA6318) and City of Joshua (JO6365). Checking the custId caught it. A code page that matches your expectation is still a page about SOME city; read which one.  2026-11-14 ANSWERED -- LOWRY CROSSING S WARDS ARE ELECTORATES, NOT RESIDENCY QUALIFICATIONS. CC_0432 left this open because R9i had settled the same question the OTHER way for South Portland. It is now settled here by the returns, two independent elections, and the test is TURNOUT rather than wording: a contest s "Contest Totals" counts the ballots that CONTAINED it (votes + overvotes + undervotes), so it measures ballot presence and not voter interest. (1) MAY 2, 2026 official canvass: City Council Ward 4 Contest Totals 22 -- i.e. 11 ballots, since it was Vote For 2 -- while city-wide Proposition A in the SAME election drew Contest Totals 177. At-large seats would have put Ward 4 on all 177. (2) NOVEMBER 3, 2026 official precinct report: four SEPARATE contests, each Vote For 1, with Contest Totals 225 / 293 / 336 / 127 for Wards 1/2/3/4. If every voter got all four they would be IDENTICAL; they are not, and they sum to ~981, which is one ward contest per voter. (3) Corroborating, the ballot s own Spanish reads "Distrito N Del Concejo Municipal". ▶ SO THE FIX IS FOUR WARD POLYGONS AND EIGHT RETITLED SEATS, NOT a repoint to the city-wide district -- which would tell every voter that all eight councilmembers represent them when they elect two. ⚠ Places 1-4 ALREADY point city-wide, so that error is live today for half the council while the other half is invisible.  ⚠ AND A SECOND JOB FELL OUT OF THE SAME RESEARCH: the 2026-11-03 election was 11 days ago and every ward had a seat up. Official countywide results: Ward 1 Derek Stephens 103 def. Bennie "B.J." Long 49; Ward 2 Cynthia Sandlin 185 unopposed; Ward 3 Cindy Cash 199 unopposed (a sitting member); Ward 4 Donna Crenshaw Outland 40 def. OLLIE SIMPSON 33 -- a SITTING member who LOST. Sandlin and Stephens are in no politicians row we hold. 🔴 A CERTIFIED RESULT IS NOT A FACT ABOUT WHO HOLDS THE SEAT and a losing incumbent still holds it until his successor takes office, so nothing is seated on this; it is recorded so the next pass does not re-derive it.  ⚠ The county s all-races CSV export and its official precinct report DISAGREE slightly for Ward 2 (297 vs 293 ballots, 186 vs 185 votes). The PDF marked official is authoritative; the CSV export is not the canvass.
